npcs.name: Ostorius Varro
npcs.greet: Don't lend me anything. Please. Not a copper, not a kind word. You don't know what happens to people I owe.

npcs.name: Jorunn Stone-Wife
npcs.greet: Bread's on the counter, stew's on the fire. If you're going north, you're going past the stones. Are you going north?

npcs.name: Galen Vinicius
npcs.greet: Weald Shiraz, the finest vintage in Colovia. Buy a bottle. Or... have you been west, into the hills? Did you hear music?

npcs.name: Priestess Ilvari Seloth
npcs.greet: Twilight keep you, outlander. Forgive me if I look past you. I am always looking south at this hour.

npcs.name: Fevyn Andalor
npcs.greet: You're not from the Council Club, are you? No. Good. They laughed at me. Will you listen, at least?

npcs.name: Mortician Mirvala Sadri
npcs.greet: Walk softly in Necrom, traveller. The dead are listening, and some of them are very cross with us this month.

npcs.name: Ri'jasha the Caravaneer
npcs.greet: This one has nothing to sell. This one had twelve wagons once. Now this one has a story, and the story is not a happy one.

npcs.name: Master Ahzirr
npcs.greet: You stand like someone who has been in a fight and won it by luck. Sit. This one will teach you to need less luck.

relics.name: Atrius Swallow-Stone
relics.desc: A palm-sized grey stone carved with a swallow in flight, black with old soot, still faintly warm.

relics.name: Ostorius's Bond-Stone
relics.desc: A smooth black pebble that is always slightly too heavy. When you hold it, you can hear coins counting themselves.

relics.name: Lens of the Dawn
relics.desc: A disc of Ayleid glass the size of a palm. Under the grime it holds a faint, stubborn light, like the sky an hour before sunrise.

relics.name: The Chain-Keeper's Keys
relics.desc: A ring of iron keys, rimed with frost, each one stamped with a tiny spiked mace.

relics.name: Lucilla's Green Masque
relics.desc: A half-mask of green silk and vine leaves, smelling of wine. Tucked behind it is a note in a girl's careful hand.

relics.name: Fulvius's Good Hat
relics.desc: A green felt hat with a heron feather, worn at a provocative angle. It is slightly singed and smells of scamp.

relics.name: The Twilight Stone of Deshaan
relics.desc: A pale moonstone the size of a fist. It is dull all day and glows softly, sadly, for the hour of dusk.

relics.name: Vial of Stolen Dreams
relics.desc: A stoppered glass vial full of something red that moves like smoke. If you put your ear to it, you can hear someone sleeping.

relics.name: Ashtusk's Crowned Tusk
relics.desc: A great kagouti tusk, snapped long ago and grown back jagged, so that its broken end looks like a crown.

relics.name: Ordinator Dral's Mask
relics.desc: The gilded face-mask of a Temple Ordinator, defaced with soot and a crude spiked crown.

relics.name: Urn of Ancestor Llaren Indavel
relics.desc: A heavy bonemold urn, cracked but sealed, painted with the sigil of the Necrom mortuary. Something inside it is very displeased.

relics.name: Lirrian's Root-Journal
relics.desc: A Mages Guild field journal swollen with Hist sap. The pages are stuck together, and the ink on them is still moving.

relics.name: The Chain-Lord's Keys
relics.desc: A ring of new iron keys on a chain stamped with the crest of a fallen Dunmer House.

relics.name: A Saxhleel Hunting Spear
relics.desc: A reed-bound spear with a bone point, the shaft carved with a family's hunting marks. It was found standing point-up in the mud.

relics.name: The Customs-Master's Strongbox
relics.desc: An Imperial strongbox crusted with two centuries of harbour mud, stamped with the eagle of the old Customs. It clinks.

relics.name: The Lady's Offering Box
relics.desc: A small ebony box carved with a hooded figure. It is heavier than it looks, and it is never quite where you left it.

relics.name: Hazadir's Notched Ring
relics.desc: A heavy silver ring with nine notches filed into the band, one for each challenger who drank his tea.

relics.name: Caravan Bell of the Clan Ra'zhan
relics.desc: A brass caravan bell on a leather strap, its clapper carved like a moon. It rings out of time, always.

relics.name: Dark-Moon Pendant
relics.desc: A pendant of black stone shaped like a moon in eclipse. It is cold, and in sunlight it casts no shadow.

quests.title: The Swallow-Stone
quests.desc: Lucia Atrius of Anvil wrote to the masons of Kvatch: her family's seal-stone, carved with a swallow, was buried under a cellar flag in the glassblowers' lane the night the Gate opened.
quests.pitch: There's a letter pinned up at the masons' table from a woman in Anvil. Her family's seal-stone is buried somewhere in the old glassblowers' lane. The masons haven't time. Maybe you have.

objectives.text: Find the old glassblowers' lane beneath the cathedral
Dig under the third flag from the hearth for the Atrius seal-stone
objectives.journal: Under the third flag, in a nest of skeevers, a grey stone with a swallow on it. It is warm, as though someone had held it a moment ago.

quests.outro: You leave the swallow-stone at the masons' table with a note for Lucia Atrius of Anvil. Savlian Matius promises it will reach her. One thing, at least, did not melt.

quests.title: Settled in Full
quests.offer: You look like a man with a debt on his mind.
quests.pitch: Debts? I have none. That's the trouble. I asked the Prince at the stones south of town to settle what I owed, and he settled it. With a roof, a chicken bone and a mule. My sister Livilla is the last name on the list. Get the bond-stone back from his shrine before he gets to her.
quests.desc: Ostorius Varro of Chorrol wished at the shrine of Clavicus Vile that his debts be settled. Every one of his creditors has died since. Only his sister remains.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Clavicus Vile south of Chorrol
Defeat the Prince's Bailiff, who collects on the bargain
objectives.journal: The bailiff unravels into smoke and the smell of old parchment. Something heavy drops into the grass where it stood.

objectives.text: Take Ostorius's bond-stone from the shrine
Bring the bond-stone to Ostorius in Chorrol
objectives.reply: Is it... still counting? Gods, I can hear it. What do I do with it? Tell me what to do.

choices.label: Smash it. Owe everyone again, and keep your sister.
choices.reply: Owe everyone again. The heirs of the dead, the widow's sons, the cobbler's apprentice. Three hundred drakes and a pair of boots. Well. Livilla lives. That is cheap at the price.

choices.label: Pay your sister her six drakes first. Then the bargain has nothing left to settle.
choices.reply: Pay her. Of course. If I owe nothing, the Prince has nothing to collect. I'll run to Skingrad tonight with six drakes in my fist and never borrow so much as a spoon again.

quests.outro: In Chorrol they say Ostorius Varro now pays for his bread before he picks it up, and won't shake hands with anyone.

quests.title: The Line of the Dead
quests.desc: Sister Aurelia Vanne kept Meridia's light on a hill north-east of the Imperial City. A necromancer named Corvus the Pale has raised the Ayleid dead beneath it and set them round the statue to smother its light.
quests.pitch: The Meridia statue past the farms has gone dark. Skeletons standing round it in a ring, and a man in black behind them. The sister who kept the light left a journal there. Someone should read it, and then do what it asks.

objectives.text: Break the ring of Ayleid dead around the statue
Kill Corvus the Pale
objectives.journal: Corvus dies cursing the light. The skeletons fold to the ground like puppets with their strings cut.

objectives.text: Lift the Lens of the Dawn from the statue's hands
objectives.journal: As you lift the lens, the grey film slides from it like ash in the rain, and a thin clean light comes up out of the glass, as if the statue had drawn breath.

quests.outro: When you set the lens back, the statue blazes for a moment so brightly that the farmers below come out of their doors to look. Meridia keeps her bargains. A sliver of Ayleid glass is waiting at the statue's feet.

quests.title: The Girl Who Sang in the Cold
quests.offer: You look like you haven't slept in days.
quests.pitch: My Hilde took bread up the north road four days ago. The watch says wolves. I found her basket by the Molag Bal stones with the bread still in it. Wolves eat bread. Whatever took her didn't. Please. I can't climb up there. I can't.
quests.desc: Jorunn Stone-Wife's daughter Hilde was taken on the north road from Bruma. Her basket was found near the shrine of Molag Bal in the Jeralls.

objectives.text: Climb to the shrine of Molag Bal north-west of Bruma
Kill the Chain-Keeper, Lady Ottilia Venn
Take the Chain-Keeper's keys and free the captives
objectives.journal: Hilde is alive, blue with cold, still humming under her breath. She takes the key from your hand and unlocks her own chain, and then the carter's beside her, before she lets herself cry.

objectives.text: Tell Jorunn in Bruma that her daughter is coming home
objectives.topic: Hilde is alive. She's walking down the north road now.
objectives.reply: Alive. Alive! Oh, Kynareth, oh, Mara... Sit. Sit down. You'll never pay for a meal in this house again. Not one. Not ever.

quests.outro: Bruma talks about little else for a week. Hilde sings in her mother's kitchen again, though she won't sing the song she was singing on the mountain.

quests.title: The Last Dance of Lucilla Vinicius
quests.offer: Music? No. Why do you ask?
quests.pitch: My daughter Lucilla followed that music into the hills on her name-day. West of the city, where the Sanguine statue stands. That was a month ago. The Count's steward told me some young people are better not sought. I'm not the Count. Find her. Or find out.
quests.desc: Galen Vinicius, a vintner of Skingrad, lost his daughter Lucilla to a revel at the shrine of Sanguine in the hills west of the city.

objectives.text: Follow the music to the shrine of Sanguine west of Skingrad
Drive off the Prince's revellers
Search the revel for any sign of Lucilla
objectives.journal: Lucilla is not here. Only her green masque, and a note behind it: 'Tell Father I'm happy. Tell him the Shiraz here is better. Tell him not to look for me, because he'd find me, and then he'd have to choose.'

objectives.text: Tell Galen Vinicius what you found
objectives.topic: I found her masque. And a note.
objectives.reply: Her masque. She sewed the leaves on herself. What... what did the note say?

choices.label: Tell him the truth: she chose to stay.
choices.reply: Chose. She chose. Well. She always did know her own mind, and never mine. I'll pour the first cup of this year's barrel on the soil for her. The Weald will know where to carry it.

choices.label: Tell him she is dead, and spare him the choice.
choices.reply: Dead. Then... then at least I can stop listening for the music. Thank you. I'll bury the masque by the vines. She'd have liked that.

quests.outro: On full-moon nights, a few Skingrad folk swear they hear a girl laughing in the vineyards. Galen Vinicius never mentions it.

quests.title: A Matter of Millinery
quests.desc: Fulvius Pell of Bravil left a formal complaint at the shrine of Sheogorath: the Mad God's scamp has stolen his good hat. He would like it back. He will pay in buttons. Also money.
quests.pitch: You heard about Fulvius's hat? The Mad God's scamp has it. Wears it at an angle, Fulvius says. He's offering a reward. Mostly buttons, I think. But some money.

objectives.text: Go to the Mad God's shrine north-west of Bravil
Defeat the Gentleman Scamp
objectives.journal: The scamp bows deeply before it dies, and the hat stays on its head the whole time, which seems unfair.

objectives.text: Recover Fulvius's good hat

quests.outro: You'll find Fulvius in Bravil eventually, or he'll find you. He'll wear the hat at exactly the same angle as the scamp did, and swear he always has.

quests.title: The Twilight Stone
quests.offer: What are you looking at, to the south?
quests.pitch: At the Lady's light, in the wrong hands. The Twilight Stone was torn from her statue east of here by Argonian raiders forty-three winters ago. I have learned where it went: to a cult of rot-eaters at the Namira stones in the Shadowfen, who light their feasts by it. I am too old to cross the border. You are not.
quests.desc: Priestess Ilvari Seloth of Mournhold wants the Twilight Stone returned to Azura's shrine. Rot-eaters at the shrine of Namira in Black Marsh's Shadowfen hold it.

objectives.text: Cross into the Shadowfen to the shrine of Namira
Kill the rot-eaters' Feastmaster
Take back the Twilight Stone
objectives.journal: The stone is dull in your hand. Then the sun touches the treeline, and it begins, very faintly, to glow.

objectives.text: Bring the Twilight Stone to Priestess Ilvari in Mournhold
objectives.topic: The Twilight Stone. It's yours again.
objectives.reply: Forty-three winters. I was a novice when they took it. Look at it, at dusk, in a Dunmer hand. The Lady has been patient with us. Tonight, at last, she will not have to be.

quests.outro: When the stone is set back in its socket, the statue east of Mournhold glows at dusk for the first time in living memory, and half the city walks out to see it.

quests.title: The Dream-Mother's Ring
quests.pitch: My brother Drals walks out of Balmora in his sleep every night, toward the Vaermina stones under the mountain. There's a ring of sleepers there, and a woman in the middle singing to them. She's drinking them. I can see it in his face. Please. Stop her.
quests.desc: Fevyn Andalor's brother Drals is one of the ash-sleepers who walk each night to the shrine of Vaermina, where a priestess called the Dream-Mother feeds on their nightmares.

objectives.text: Follow the sleepers to the shrine of Vaermina under Red Mountain
Kill the Dream-Mother
objectives.journal: When the Dream-Mother falls, the ring of sleepers sways like grass in the wind, and then they all sit down at once, still sleeping.

objectives.text: Take the vial of stolen dreams from her body
Bring the vial to Fevyn in Balmora
objectives.topic: The Dream-Mother is dead. I have this vial. Drals's dreams are in it.
objectives.reply: His dreams. All the nights he's lost. If I break it, will he wake? If I give them back to him... will he remember what she showed him?

choices.label: Break the vial. Let him wake empty, but free.
choices.reply: Then he'll wake not knowing the last year. Not knowing he walked, not knowing I wept. Maybe that's a mercy. He'll think I just got old.

choices.label: Give it to him. They are his dreams, even the bad ones.
choices.reply: They're his. Even the mountain, even the fire. He'll scream, the first night. And then he'll be Drals again, all of him. I'll sit up with him. I've had practice.

quests.outro: The sleepers of Balmora stop walking, for now. The Temple calls it a blessing. Fevyn Andalor calls it you.

quests.title: The Crowned Tusk
quests.desc: Hircine has marked his prey for the season on Azura's Coast: a bull kagouti called Ashtusk, with one tusk snapped into a crown. The Huntsman's rules: your own hand, and the tusk, not the head.
quests.pitch: The Telvanni huntsman posted a challenge at the Hircine altar west of Sadrith Mora. Some monster of a kagouti, Ashtusk. Four hunters dead. Go and read the rules before you try it. The Huntsman cares about the rules.

objectives.text: Go to the Huntsman's altar on Azura's Coast
Hunt down Ashtusk
objectives.journal: Ashtusk goes down hard, and for a moment the scrub is silent. Then, far off, something howls. It sounds pleased.

objectives.text: Take the crowned tusk, as the Huntsman's rules demand

quests.outro: Ulath Morvel pays, as promised, and asks you to sign his hunting book. Ashlander trackers nod to you on the coast road now, as one hunter to another.

quests.title: The Unbroken Ash
quests.desc: A cult calling itself the Unbroken Ash holds the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon west of Necrom. Its speaker, Sul Indaram, killed Ordinator Dral and wears his mask at the rites. The Ordinators of Necrom ask for outside help.
quests.pitch: Four Ordinators came back from the Dagon stones. The fifth's mask is on a heretic's face now. The Temple won't say it, but they're asking for help. Read their report at the shrine, if you dare go that close.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Mehrunes Dagon in Molag Amur
Break the cultists of the Unbroken Ash and their summoned dremora
Kill Sul Indaram, speaker of the Unbroken Ash
objectives.journal: Indaram dies looking at the statue, not at you. He looks almost relieved.

objectives.text: Recover Ordinator Dral's mask

quests.outro: The Ordinators of Necrom take Dral's mask without a word, clean it, and lay it in the mortuary. One of them, later, buys you a drink, and still says nothing, which is high praise from an Ordinator.

quests.title: The Displeased Ancestor
quests.desc: Grave-robbers have broken urns in Necrom's catacombs and sold the ashes to Daedra-worshippers. Mortician Mirvala Sadri wants the urn of the mortuary's founder, Llaren Indavel, brought home from the robbers' camp behind the Mad God's shrine.
quests.pitch: Somebody's stealing our dead. The mortician's frantic, and old Llaren's urn is gone, the founder himself. The robbers camp behind the Mad God's shrine on the pilgrim road. Mirvala at the mortuary will pay. Llaren won't, but he'll stop rattling the walls.

objectives.text: Find the grave-robbers' camp behind the Mad God's shrine
Kill Vedam the Urn-Breaker and his gang
Recover the urn of Ancestor Llaren Indavel
objectives.journal: The urn is cracked but sealed. As you lift it, it grows heavier, then lighter, as if someone inside had decided you would do.

objectives.text: Return the urn to Mortician Mirvala in Necrom
objectives.reply: Oh, thank the Three. And thank you. Listen. Do you hear that? Nothing. For the first time in a month, the catacombs are quiet. He approves of you. That is not a small thing. He approves of almost no one.

quests.outro: Your name is written, small, in the margin of the mortuary's book of benefactors. The priests say that in Necrom, the dead read the margins.

quests.title: What the Root Remembers
quests.desc: Adrienne Lirrian of the Gideon Mages Guild studied a Hist root that has grown through the shrine of Hermaeus Mora west of Stormhold. She tasted the sap and was lost. Her assistant Kassus guards the root, reciting secrets that are not his.
quests.pitch: The Mages Guild in Gideon wants a lost scholar's journal back. It's at the Mora stones west of Stormhold, under a Hist root, and her assistant's sitting on it, out of his mind. Don't read the journal, they say. Everybody reads the journal.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Hermaeus Mora where the Hist root grows
Stop Kassus the Unread
objectives.journal: Kassus dies reciting. The last thing he says is your own name, and the day you were born, and a thing you have never told anyone.

objectives.text: Take Lirrian's journal from beneath the root

quests.outro: Guildmaster Cyrus Aemilius of Gideon will take the journal, sealed in lead, and pay what was promised. He'll ask if you read it. Whatever you say, he will not believe you.

quests.title: Iron in the Shadowfen
quests.desc: Varis Hlervu, a Dunmer of a fallen House who calls himself the Chain-Lord, holds Saxhleel captives in chains at the shrine of Molag Bal near the Necrom border, as an offering to the Prince of Domination.
quests.pitch: Helstrom's asking for every spear. There's a Dunmer at the Molag Bal stones on the border with nine of ours in new chains. Calls himself the Chain-Lord. Says his Prince promised him our hides. Show him what the marsh promises.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Molag Bal in the Shadowfen
Cut down the Chain-Lord's hirelings
Kill Varis Hlervu, the Chain-Lord
Take the Chain-Lord's keys and free the captives
objectives.journal: You unlock nine sets of chains. The Saxhleel do not thank you in words. They walk south toward Helstrom together, and the last of them touches your arm as he passes.

quests.outro: The warriors of Helstrom carry the Chain-Lord's chains home and drop them into the black pool. They drop a stone in, too, for you. It is a great honour, they assure you, though you are still alive.

quests.title: Hunt the Hunter
quests.desc: A Legion deserter cursed with Hircine's blood hunts Saxhleel hunters in the Shadowfen and plants their spears at the Huntsman's statue east of Cheydinhal. Sings-in-Reeds, whose brother was among them, asks for the hunter to be hunted.
quests.pitch: Five spears stuck in the mud at the Huntsman's stones, points up. A wolf that was a legionnaire put them there. One of them belonged to Sings-in-Reeds's brother. The Huntsman likes a fair hunt. This isn't one. Make it one.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Hircine in the Shadowfen
Kill the Legion Wolf
objectives.journal: When the wolf dies, it becomes a man again: an Imperial, young, with a Legion tattoo on his wrist and a look of terrible relief.

objectives.text: Pull the spears from the mud and take the brother's spear

quests.outro: You plant the brother's spear point-down at the statue, as the Saxhleel do for a hunt fairly ended. By morning there is a feather beside it.

quests.title: The Customs-Master's Strongbox
quests.desc: The last Imperial customs-master of Lilmoth sank his strongbox of thirty years' bribes off the old customs pier when the Empire left. His letter says where. The slaughterfish have kept it ever since.
quests.pitch: Every diver in Lilmoth's gone after that old Imperial strongbox. It's off the end of the customs pier, in the shadow of the harbour tower. The fish there are the size of dogs. Bring a long hook and a short temper.

objectives.text: Find the end of the old customs pier in Lilmoth harbour
Raise the customs-master's strongbox from the mud
objectives.journal: The strongbox comes up black with mud and heavier than any honest box should be. Two centuries of bribes, and every coin stamped with a dead Emperor's face.

quests.outro: The Saxhleel dock-workers watch you open the box and laugh until they have to sit down. 'Imperial gold,' one says, 'paid to an Imperial, to cheat the marsh. And now the marsh gives it to you.' He seems to think that is the best joke in Lilmoth.

quests.title: Rajhin's Bow
quests.desc: A gang called the Shadow-Claws robbed the shrine of Nocturnal near Senchal, taking the offerings and the bow that Rajhin the Footpad himself hung at the Lady's feet. Old Ja'khirr, the Last Footpad, asks for the offerings to be returned.
quests.pitch: The Shadow-Claws robbed the Lady. Took Rajhin's own bow. Old Ja'khirr left a message at the stones for whoever's brave enough. Every thief in Senchal is cheering for you. Quietly. From very far away.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Nocturnal near Senchal
Deal with the Shadow-Claws mocking the Lady at her stones
Kill Jo'vahn the Unlucky
objectives.journal: Jo'vahn's last words are 'this one should have stayed a pickpocket'. Fair.

objectives.text: Return the Lady's offering box to the shrine
objectives.journal: When you set the box at the statue's feet, its lid opens by itself. The coins and rings are inside. The bow is not. It is lying across your pack, as if it had always been there.

quests.outro: The thieves of Senchal will never say your name aloud. They will, however, never steal from you either, and in Senchal that is a kind of knighthood.

quests.title: Refuse the Tea
quests.desc: Hazadir the Unbowed holds the shrine of Boethra in the Pellitine hills and has killed nine challengers, each after a cup of poisoned tea. His old master, Ahzirr, wants him stopped and his notched ring brought to Riverhold.
quests.pitch: Hazadir at the Boethra stones has killed nine. All after tea. His old master's left a letter there for anyone who'll fight him. Here's the trick, friend: don't drink the tea.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Boethra in Pellitine and challenge Hazadir
Refuse the tea, and defeat Hazadir the Unbowed
objectives.journal: Hazadir offers you tea. You decline. For a moment he looks almost proud of you, and then he draws.

objectives.text: Take Hazadir's notched ring
Bring the ring to Master Ahzirr in Riverhold
objectives.topic: Hazadir is dead. Here is his ring.
objectives.reply: Nine notches. Ja'rasha. Do'kirr. Little Zahra... This one will file them off one at a time and say each name. Then this one will melt the ring and make a teacup of it. Boethra likes a joke, and so did Hazadir, once.

quests.outro: Master Ahzirr's students bow to you in the streets of Riverhold, very deeply. You have learned enough by now to notice they are measuring your stance.

quests.title: The Bell of the Ra'zhan
quests.pitch: The Taskmaster happened. We stopped for water at the Peryite stones north of the city and this one's cousins caught his orderly plague. They walk in rows around the statue now, counting. This one cannot save them. But the clan's bell is on the lead wagon, and without it the Ra'zhan cannot call their dead home to the Lattice. Bring this one the bell.
quests.desc: Ri'jasha's caravan of the clan Ra'zhan caught Peryite's orderly plague at the shrine north of Torval. She wants the clan's caravan bell brought back, so her people can one day be called home.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Peryite north of Torval
Drive off the plague-rats swarming the wagons
Take the caravan bell from the lead wagon
objectives.journal: When you lift the bell it rings once, out of time, and every one of the counting Khajiit stops and looks up at the moons, just for a breath, before they begin again.

objectives.text: Bring the bell to Ri'jasha in Torval
objectives.topic: Your clan's bell. And... they looked up, when it rang.
objectives.reply: They looked up? Then they are still in there, somewhere under the counting. This one will take the bell to the Moon-Bishop. Perhaps the Lattice can call louder than the Taskmaster. Perhaps. This one will ring it every night until it does.

quests.outro: Every evening in Torval's market, a single caravan bell rings out of time. The Moon-Priests have begun to ring their own bells with it.

quests.title: The Moonless Son
quests.desc: Za'mira's son J'kar stole a dark-moon pendant from the Dro-m'Athra at the shrine of Namiira and has walked with them ever since. His mother asks that the pendant be taken from him and brought into the light, whatever it costs.
quests.pitch: Old Za'mira left a letter at Namiira's stones for her son. J'kar walks with the dark-souled now. She wants the pendant off him, even if he has to die for it. Go by night. That's when they gather.

objectives.text: Go to the shrine of Namiira north-west of Torval
End J'kar the Moonless, and the dark-souled who walk with him
objectives.journal: J'kar falls, and for a moment, before the end, his eyes clear. He says 'tell Mother I'm sorry about the window'.

objectives.text: Take the dark-moon pendant out into the light

quests.outro: Za'mira buries her son with a candle burning, so he can see the way home. The Moon-Priests take the pendant and say they will drop it in the deepest well in Torval, where no moon has ever shone.
